variables.policy_prompt_for_subgoal: First update remaining_path according to the policy prompt for memory. If its first letter is A, select A: move to the nearest robot-left target clockwise. If B, select B: move to the nearest robot-right target clockwise. If C, select C: move to the nearest robot-left target counterclockwise. If D, select D: move to the nearest robot-right target counterclockwise. These conditions apply regardless of the preceding subgoal: after any completed A, B, C, or D, transition to whichever letter now leads remaining_path. The current highlighted target is the departure site, not the destination. Robot-left selects the adjacent target with larger x and robot-right the adjacent target with smaller x; the menu handles these targets internally and requires no point. Initial subgoals decoded from the demonstrations are B for episode 0, A for episode 19, D for episode 58, A for episode 86, and A for episode 99. Never infer the next direction solely from the current location: identical locations can require different moves on repeated visits. If the list is empty, the demonstrated route is complete and no further traversal is intended. If an unexpected situation nevertheless requires a menu answer, or the demonstration cannot be decoded, choose A if a larger-x adjacent target exists, otherwise B if a smaller-x adjacent target exists, otherwise A; this is only a deterministic fallback, not an additional demonstrated move.

fields.name: remaining_path
fields.description: When memory is empty and demonstration frames are present, decode all demonstration traversals and write their menu letters in chronological order. Segment at arrivals at adjacent target sites, using highlight changes together with wrist arrival; merge small coordinate fluctuations and temporary double highlights into the same target identity. Preserve every repeated traversal and reversal. Destination x larger than departure x is robot-left, and smaller x is robot-right. Determine the arc from intermediate wrist positions relative to the line joining the wrist resting positions at the departure and arrival sites: image-upper leftward is A, image-lower rightward is B, image-lower leftward is C, and image-upper rightward is D. Do not confuse the wrist with the attached stick endpoint or treat the wrist's offset from target coordinates as evidence of arc direction. Write the full list at this first decision, without deleting the move selected now. On a later decision with carried memory, the intervening execution shows the preceding oracle command completed at its adjacent target; remove exactly one leading letter from the carried list before selecting the next command. The decision-step protocol guarantees that each such return follows one completed command, so do not count individual frames or repeated highlights as additional completions. If there is no intervening completed execution, retain the carried list. Once exhausted, write []. e.g. ["A","B","A","D"]
fields.annotation: An ordered list of menu letters encoding the demonstrated traversals not yet completed in execution, including the traversal to command at this decision step. Decode the demonstration into individual moves between adjacent target sites, preserving repeated visits and reversals. Larger destination x means robot-left; smaller destination x means robot-right. A leftward move along the image-upper arc is A, a rightward move along the image-lower arc is B, a leftward move along the image-lower arc is C, and a rightward move along the image-upper arc is D. Judge the arc from the intermediate wrist trajectory relative to the line joining its resting positions at the two target sites, not by comparing wrist height directly with target coordinates. Target highlight changes identify arrivals; small coordinate fluctuations and briefly simultaneous highlights do not constitute extra moves. At the first execution decision, record the entire decoded demonstration. At each subsequent decision, remove the single leading move completed during the intervening oracle execution. Do not remove the move being chosen at the current decision. Thus episode 0 has ["B","B"] then ["B"]; episode 19 has ["A","B","A","D"], ["B","A","D"], ["A","D"], ["D"]; episode 58 has ["D","D","A","A"], ["D","A","A"], ["A","A"], ["A"]; episode 86 has ["A","C","A","B","D"], ["C","A","B","D"], ["A","B","D"], ["B","D"], ["D"]; episode 99 has ["A","B","C","D"], ["B","C","D"], ["C","D"], ["D"]. After the final traversal completes, the value is []. e.g. ["A","B","A","D"]
